metadata.research_goal: Deep research draft for tennis injury risk, strength and conditioning, load management, readiness, and return-to-tennis rules that can be converted into backend planning records.
scope: serve count and high-intent serve count
shoulder, elbow, wrist, trunk, low-back, hip, knee, ankle, calf, and Achilles load
youth growth and older adult contexts
rotational power, medicine ball, and plyometrics

key_concepts.name: Tennis load must be tracked by anatomical and technical channels
key_concepts.summary: A useful tennis backend should separate serve load, high-intent serve load, forehand volume, backhand volume, overhead volume, sprint/deceleration/COD density, surface exposure, gym load, match density, and next-day joint response.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create separate load counters instead of one generic session duration score.

key_concepts.name: External load only matters when paired with internal response
key_concepts.summary: Serve counts, stroke counts, sprints, minutes, and matches should be paired with pain, soreness, energy, sleep, range of motion, and next-day readiness because the same external load can affect players differently.
key_concepts.backend_use: Store external_load_fields and internal_response_fields on session summaries.

key_concepts.name: Serve is a distinct high-load stroke family
key_concepts.summary: The serve combines leg drive, trunk extension and rotation, shoulder external/internal rotation, elbow extension, forearm pronation, wrist motion, landing, and recovery. It should not be counted as equivalent to groundstroke volume.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create serve_count and high_intent_serve_count fields independent from total hitting volume.

key_concepts.name: High-intent serves are a separate exposure class
key_concepts.summary: First serves, maximal-velocity serves, heavy kick serves, and pressure-point serves create greater trunk, shoulder, elbow, wrist, abdominal, and landing demand than technical shadow serves or submaximal placement serves.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use high_intent_serve_count as the primary acute upper-body and trunk spike flag.

key_concepts.name: Efficient kinetic-chain transfer reduces local overload
key_concepts.summary: Tennis strokes depend on coordinated force transfer from legs and hips through trunk, scapula, arm, forearm, wrist, and racket. Breakdowns in legs, trunk, scapula, or timing can push excess load to the shoulder, elbow, wrist, or lumbar spine.
key_concepts.backend_use: Attach technique-risk flags to load rules, especially for serve, forehand, and one-handed backhand.

key_concepts.name: Tennis is a repeated braking and reacceleration sport
key_concepts.summary: Court movement is dominated by short accelerations, lateral recovery, braking, split-step timing, change of direction, and repeated restart demands rather than continuous running.
key_concepts.backend_use: Conditioning records should prescribe tennis-shaped repeat efforts and deceleration capacity, not only generic steady-state or random HIIT.

key_concepts.name: Surface changes tactical and tissue load
key_concepts.summary: Clay, grass, and hard courts change bounce, rally length, sliding or braking style, plantar pressure, lower-limb impact, and movement rhythm. Surface should modify conditioning, warm-up, footwear, and recovery planning.
key_concepts.backend_use: Add surface as a required context for match, session, and tournament load records.

key_concepts.name: Tournament density is a recovery and injury-risk context
key_concepts.summary: Multiple matches across consecutive days compress recovery time and can stack serve, groundstroke, change-of-direction, and psychological load even if each match looks tolerable in isolation.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create competition_density flags from matches_in_7_days, matches_in_48_hours, and projected next match.

key_concepts.name: Youth growth and maturation alter load tolerance
key_concepts.summary: Junior players need staged development, growth-spurt awareness, movement quality, recovery, and careful volume progression because maturation changes coordination, tendon-bone stress, and fatigue response.
key_concepts.backend_use: Add growth_spurt_status and maturation_notes to youth planning gates where available.

key_concepts.name: Older adult tennis needs capacity and recovery buffers
key_concepts.summary: Veteran tennis can support health and fitness, but planning should respect lower recovery reserve, prior joint history, tendon stiffness, balance, warm-up time, and progressive strength/power exposure.
key_concepts.backend_use: Add older_adult modifiers for warm-up duration, load progression, recovery spacing, balance, and tendon capacity.

key_concepts.name: Readiness should be traffic-lighted from pain, function, and trend
key_concepts.summary: Green, yellow, and red readiness states should combine pain during play, next-day response, swelling, range of motion, confidence, sleep/fatigue, and recent load spikes.
key_concepts.backend_use: Return one readiness_status and specific load modifications from readiness rules.

key_concepts.name: Return to tennis is a continuum, not a binary clearance
key_concepts.summary: Return should progress from participation, to controlled tennis practice, to competitive tennis, to full performance with staged serve, stroke, movement, and match-density exposure.
key_concepts.backend_use: Create staged return_to_tennis records with pass criteria and progression caps.

technical_models.name: Serve load sequence
model: racket drop and shoulder external rotation
contact with shoulder internal rotation, elbow extension, forearm pronation, and wrist contribution
technical_models.risk_logic: High volumes or abrupt spikes in high-intent serves stress the shoulder, elbow, wrist, abdominal wall, low back, landing leg, and calf/Achilles chain.

technical_models.name: Shoulder and scapular durability model
technical_models.model: Track shoulder load through serve and overhead volume, racket acceleration intent, scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, trunk contribution, and next-day ache or ROM change.
technical_models.risk_logic: When trunk or scapular contribution is insufficient, the shoulder may absorb more repetitive acceleration and deceleration demand.

technical_models.name: Elbow and forearm load model
technical_models.model: Elbow load rises with high-intent serving, late contact, heavy topspin, grip stress, one-handed backhand stress, forearm fatigue, and rapid changes in racket or string setup.
technical_models.risk_logic: Elbow symptoms should trigger reductions in high-intent serve and high-volume heavy-spin hitting while forearm, shoulder, trunk, and technique factors are addressed.

technical_models.name: Wrist load model
technical_models.model: Wrist exposure should account for forehand/backhand volume, extreme grips, heavy spin, late or jammed contact, return impact, volley block volume, and ball-striking intensity.
technical_models.risk_logic: Wrist tendinopathy risk rises when repetitive stroke volume and impact increase faster than forearm and wrist capacity.

technical_models.name: Trunk and low-back rotation model
technical_models.model: Track trunk load through serve count, kick serve count, forehand/backhand rotation volume, open-stance repetition, defensive stretch hits, medicine-ball volume, and fatigue-related loss of hip contribution.
technical_models.risk_logic: Low-back and abdominal issues are more likely when rotation, extension, and lateral flexion volume spike or when hips and trunk cannot share force efficiently.

technical_models.name: Forehand and backhand volume model
technical_models.model: Forehand and backhand load should be counted separately because stance, grip, contact height, spin, stroke side, and one-handed versus two-handed mechanics change tissue stress.
technical_models.risk_logic: High forehand volume can increase shoulder, wrist, trunk, hip, and open-stance loading; backhand volume can stress wrist, elbow, trunk, and front-side braking depending on technique.

technical_models.name: Sprint, deceleration, and COD density model
technical_models.model: Track repeated short accelerations, lateral shuffles, crossover recoveries, hard stops, wide-ball braking events, and direction changes per minute or per drill.
technical_models.risk_logic: High COD density with poor braking mechanics increases hip, knee, ankle, calf, Achilles, and low-back stress.

technical_models.name: Lower-limb tendon chain model
technical_models.model: Hip, knee, ankle, calf, and Achilles risk should be modeled from acceleration, braking, jumping, landing, sliding, surface stiffness, footwear change, and plyometric/gym exposure.
technical_models.risk_logic: Tendon and joint symptoms often reflect cumulative changes in load, surface, and recovery rather than one isolated session.

technical_models.name: Surface adjustment model
technical_models.model: Hard court should flag impact and braking load; clay should flag longer rallies, sliding exposure, adductor/hip/calf control, and higher movement volume; grass should flag low bounce, reaction time, slipping, and hamstring/calf readiness.
technical_models.risk_logic: Changing surfaces rapidly is a load change even if total tennis minutes do not increase.

technical_models.name: Readiness input model
technical_models.model: Readiness should combine symptom severity, next-day response, joint swelling, range of motion, movement quality, fatigue, sleep, mood, recent load spike, and competition density.
technical_models.risk_logic: A single readiness score hides the reason load should change; backend rules should expose the limiting input.

technical_models.name: Return-to-tennis staged exposure model
model: medical or clinical clearance where needed
pain-free daily function and baseline strength/mobility
progressive serve reintroduction from low intent to high intent
technical_models.risk_logic: Serve, high-speed movement, reactive play, and tournament density should return after basic function and controlled hitting tolerate next-day checks.

technical_models.name: Rotational medicine-ball power model
technical_models.model: Rotational throws should progress from low-volume, controlled hip-trunk sequencing to faster tennis-specific throws, with throws separated from peak serve-load days if trunk or shoulder risk is elevated.
technical_models.risk_logic: Medicine-ball work can train useful rotational power but adds trunk, shoulder, elbow, wrist, and landing load when volume or intent spikes.

technical_models.name: Plyometric and landing-dose model
technical_models.model: Plyometric training should be tracked by contacts, intensity, direction, surface, landing quality, and proximity to match play because tennis already includes repeated jump, split-step, and braking contacts.
technical_models.risk_logic: Plyometric work can improve speed and power, but should be reduced when Achilles, patellar tendon, calf, ankle, knee, or growth-related symptoms are present.

tactical_rules.name: Elbow pain tactical substitution
tactical_rules.action: Reduce high-intent serves, heavy topspin forehands, and one-handed backhand volume; bias cooperative rally tolerance, return blocking, footwork, and lower-intensity placement serving.
tactical_rules.why: Elbow symptoms should not be paired with maximal serve, high spin, and high racket-impact exposure in the same microcycle.

tactical_rules.name: Shoulder pain overhead-load cap
tactical_rules.action: Remove maximal serving, overhead smashes, and high-volume return drills; use submaximal technical serves only if pain remains green and next-day response is stable.
tactical_rules.why: Shoulder overload may worsen when serve and overhead volume continue despite pain or range-of-motion change.

tactical_rules.name: Low-back rotation modifier
tactical_rules.action: Reduce kick serves, maximal trunk-rotation medicine-ball throws, open-stance power drilling, defensive wide-ball hitting, and fatigue-based point play.
tactical_rules.why: Low-back symptoms need reduced extension-rotation volume while hip mobility, trunk endurance, and controlled stroke mechanics are restored.

tactical_rules.name: Wrist pain contact-quality rule
tactical_rules.action: Reduce high-spin, late-contact, high-pace return, and jammed-volley work; prioritize cleaner contact spacing, lower ball speed, and forearm/wrist capacity work.
tactical_rules.why: Wrist symptoms are sensitive to repetitive stroke volume, impact, grip mechanics, and late contact.

tactical_rules.name: Serve plus forehand spike guard
tactical_rules.condition: high_intent_serve_count increased > 25% week_to_week and forehand_count increased > 25% week_to_week
tactical_rules.action: Do not add a maximal upper-body gym or rotational power day; keep next session technical, lower-volume, or movement-quality focused.
tactical_rules.why: Stacking high-intent serve and forehand volume with upper-body loading creates an avoidable shoulder, elbow, wrist, trunk, and hip-load cluster.

tactical_rules.name: Match-day minus one load rule
tactical_rules.action: Keep high-intent serve count low to moderate, avoid novel plyometric or heavy eccentric lower-body work, rehearse patterns, and end with recovery and mobility.
tactical_rules.why: The day before competition should preserve freshness and avoid novel soreness while retaining rhythm and confidence.

tactical_rules.name: Same-day multiple-match rule
tactical_rules.action: Prioritize hydration, refueling, shade/cooling as needed, low-volume mobility, light rhythm hits only, and defer S&C or extra serve reps.
tactical_rules.why: Compressed recovery between matches requires energy restoration and symptom monitoring more than added training load.

tactical_rules.name: Hard-court impact gate
tactical_rules.action: Reduce hard decelerations, lateral plyometrics, jump contacts, and long point-play blocks; use lower-impact conditioning or technical hitting as needed.
tactical_rules.why: Hard court can increase impact and braking stress, so lower-limb symptoms should alter movement dose.

tactical_rules.name: Clay sliding progression
tactical_rules.action: Introduce sliding as a technical progression before high-volume live points; build hip, adductor, calf, and trunk control before long defensive rallies.
tactical_rules.why: Clay changes movement strategy and can increase sliding and longer-rally demands, especially after a surface switch.

tactical_rules.name: Grass reaction and slip guard
tactical_rules.action: Warm up calves, hamstrings, groin, and balance; emphasize lower ready position, shorter adjustment steps, controlled first-step drills, and footwear check before maximal point play.
tactical_rules.why: Low and skidding bounce changes reaction time, posture, and slip risk.

tactical_rules.name: Youth growth-spurt load modifier
tactical_rules.action: Reduce abrupt spikes in serve volume, plyometrics, long defensive rallies, and maximal COD drills; emphasize movement quality, coordination, mobility, strength basics, and recovery.
tactical_rules.why: Maturation changes coordination and tissue load tolerance, so growth periods need conservative progression.

tactical_rules.name: Older adult recovery-spacing rule
tactical_rules.action: Increase warm-up time, avoid stacking high-intent serve and high-impact movement on consecutive days, and schedule strength, mobility, and balance support around tennis.
tactical_rules.why: Older players often need longer tissue preparation and recovery spacing while still benefiting from progressive strength and power training.

tactical_rules.name: Green readiness rule
tactical_rules.condition: pain_score <= 2 and no_swelling == true and no_rom_loss == true and next_day_response == 'baseline' and fatigue_score <= 3
tactical_rules.action: Proceed with planned session; keep normal technique quality checks and avoid unnecessary novelty during dense competition weeks.
tactical_rules.why: Low stable symptoms and normal next-day response support planned progression.

tactical_rules.name: Yellow readiness rule
tactical_rules.condition: pain_score == 3 or pain_score == 4 or next_day_response == 'mildly_worse' or fatigue_score >= 4
tactical_rules.action: Reduce high-intent serve, maximal sprint/COD, plyometrics, and long point-play volume by 25-50%; choose technical quality, controlled hitting, mobility, or aerobic recovery.
tactical_rules.why: Moderate symptoms or fatigue should trigger a load adjustment without automatically removing all tennis exposure.

tactical_rules.name: Red readiness rule
tactical_rules.condition: pain_score >= 5 or sharp_pain == true or swelling == true or rom_loss == true or limping == true or neurological_symptoms == true
tactical_rules.action: Stop aggravating tennis load, remove high-intent serve and reactive movement, and recommend qualified medical assessment before return progression.
tactical_rules.why: High pain, swelling, function loss, or neurological signs exceed self-managed training modification.

tactical_rules.name: Return-stage progression rule
tactical_rules.condition: return_stage_completed == true and next_day_response == 'baseline' for 2 consecutive exposures
tactical_rules.action: Progress one exposure variable at a time: duration, intensity, serve intent, reactive movement, point pressure, or match density.
tactical_rules.why: Return-to-sport progression is safer when exposure changes are staged and monitored.

physical_demands.name: Repeated short acceleration
physical_demands.description: Tennis movement repeatedly asks for explosive first steps over short distances rather than long continuous sprinting.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Use short court-start drills, split-step to first-step work, and repeat-effort recovery matched to rally/rest rhythm.

physical_demands.name: Deceleration and braking
physical_demands.description: Wide-ball defense, recovery, approach, and direction changes create repeated braking load through hip, knee, ankle, calf, Achilles, and trunk.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Train landing, braking angles, eccentric strength, and controlled COD before chaotic live-ball volume.

physical_demands.name: Lateral change of direction
physical_demands.description: Baseline exchange demands lateral movement, split-step timing, shuffle, crossover recovery, and repeated lateral-to-forward transitions.
physical_demands.planning_implication: COD density should be counted in live points, basket drills, and conditioning blocks.

physical_demands.name: Rotational power
physical_demands.description: Serve, forehand, backhand, and open-stance hitting require hip-trunk separation, trunk stiffness, sequential rotation, and controlled deceleration.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Include medicine-ball throws, cable/lift patterns, anti-rotation work, and hip mobility based on readiness.

physical_demands.name: Shoulder and arm deceleration
physical_demands.description: Serve and overhead strokes require rapid arm acceleration and then controlled deceleration of the shoulder, elbow, forearm, and wrist.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Rotator cuff, scapular, posterior shoulder, forearm, and trunk endurance should support serve progression.

physical_demands.name: Anaerobic repeat-effort ability
physical_demands.description: Points include bursts of intense movement and stroke actions with incomplete but meaningful recovery between points.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Use interval formats that resemble tennis work-rest patterns and include technical quality constraints.

physical_demands.name: Aerobic recovery base
physical_demands.description: Aerobic fitness supports between-point recovery, repeat-match recovery, heat tolerance, and tournament durability.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Prescribe aerobic base and recovery conditioning without replacing tennis-specific speed and power needs.

physical_demands.name: Tendon stiffness and capacity
physical_demands.description: Split steps, serve landings, lateral hops, hard stops, and repeated starts load the patellar tendon, Achilles, calf, and plantar structures.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Progress calf, soleus, quadriceps, hamstring, glute, and plyometric exposure with surface and symptoms in mind.

physical_demands.name: Reactive perception-action demand
physical_demands.description: Players move and strike based on opponent, ball flight, spin, score, and surface rather than pre-planned movement only.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Return stages should move from closed drills to cooperative rally to reactive point play and then match pressure.

physical_demands.name: Surface-specific footwork
physical_demands.description: Clay, grass, and hard courts alter traction, sliding, braking, bounce, reaction time, and rally rhythm.
physical_demands.planning_implication: Add surface-specific warm-ups and movement progressions before full-intensity points after a surface change.

injury_or_load_risks.load_response: Reduce high-intent serve and overhead count; maintain pain-free mobility, cuff/scapular endurance, and low-intent technical work only if symptoms remain green.
Cut high-intent serves and heavy-spin volume first; retain lower-load footwork, tactical, and cooperative rally drills as tolerated.
Reduce stroke-impact volume, return pace, and high-spin drills; add grip/contact-quality checks and forearm capacity work.
Remove high-intent serve and maximal rotation; progress trunk isometrics, controlled rotation, then staged serve reintroduction.
Reduce serve and rotation volume; emphasize hip mobility, trunk endurance, controlled footwork, and gradual reactivity.
Reduce sliding and wide-ball drills; train hip strength, adductor capacity, trunk control, and progressive lateral movement.
Manage plyometric contacts and hard decelerations; build quadriceps, calf, glute, landing, and tendon capacity.
Use bracing/taping if clinically indicated, proprioception, landing mechanics, and progressive COD before full live points.

drivers: older age or sudden training return
injury_or_load_risks.load_response: Reduce jump contacts and hard COD; use pain-monitored calf and Achilles strengthening with gradual tennis return.
Add adaptation sessions and reduce first-week intensity after a surface change.
Shift to recovery, refueling, low-volume rhythm, and readiness checks between matches.

early_signals: loss of appetite or sleep disruption
injury_or_load_risks.load_response: Reduce volume spikes, rotate skills, protect recovery, and monitor growth-related soreness closely.
Increase warm-up, build strength and tendon capacity, avoid consecutive high-impact days, and use conservative progression.

training_implications.name: Warm-up is a required readiness intervention
training_implications.recommendation: Before tennis, use progressive pulse-raising work, dynamic mobility, activation, split-step/footwork rehearsal, progressive groundstrokes, and progressive serve build-up.
training_implications.backend_rule: Every tennis session should include warmup_block_id unless user explicitly logs independent warm-up.

training_implications.name: Cooldown and recovery should be planned after high-load sessions
training_implications.recommendation: After hard matches or intense sessions, prioritize low-intensity movement, mobility, hydration, carbohydrate and protein refueling, sleep, and symptom logging.
training_implications.backend_rule: Attach cooldown_recovery_block when session_rpe >= 7, match_play == true, or matches_today >= 1.

training_implications.name: Strength is a primary injury-risk reduction quality
training_implications.recommendation: Build lower-body, trunk, shoulder/scapular, and forearm strength progressively; do not rely only on stretching or conditioning for injury prevention.
training_implications.backend_rule: Weekly plans should include age- and level-appropriate strength support unless blocked by readiness.

training_implications.name: Rotational power needs staged progression
training_implications.recommendation: Progress trunk and hip sequencing from controlled anti-rotation and cable work to medicine-ball throws and tennis-specific high-speed rotation.
training_implications.backend_rule: Medicine-ball throw count should not increase in the same week as a large high-intent serve spike.

training_implications.name: Medicine-ball dose counts as tennis-relevant load
training_implications.recommendation: Count rotational throws, overhead throws, and scoop throws as trunk and shoulder load; adjust if abdominal, shoulder, elbow, wrist, or low-back symptoms appear.
training_implications.backend_rule: Add med_ball_rotational_throw_count to trunk and upper-body weekly load summaries.

training_implications.name: Plyometrics need contact-count and symptom gates
training_implications.recommendation: Start with low contacts and high landing quality, then progress direction, speed, reactivity, and density. Reduce dose for tendon pain, growth-spurt flags, or tournament weeks.
training_implications.backend_rule: Track plyometric_contacts and lateral_plyometric_contacts as separate lower-limb load fields.

training_implications.name: Deceleration capacity should precede chaotic point volume
training_implications.recommendation: Teach braking posture, hip/knee/ankle alignment, trunk control, and recovery steps before dense live-ball wide-court drills.
training_implications.backend_rule: Gate high COD sessions behind movement_quality_status and lower_limb_readiness.

training_implications.name: Serve load should ramp from low intent to high intent
training_implications.recommendation: Progress serve after injury or layoff from shadow rhythm to low-intent placement, moderate-intent targets, limited high-intent serves, then full serve games.
training_implications.backend_rule: Use separate caps for total_serve_count and high_intent_serve_count.

training_implications.name: Avoid stacking peak upper- and lower-body load blindly
training_implications.recommendation: Do not combine peak high-intent serve volume, high forehand volume, rotational medicine-ball work, heavy upper-body gym, hard-court COD, and plyometrics without readiness and recovery support.
training_implications.backend_rule: Flag high_load_cluster when three or more peak load channels occur within 48 hours.

training_implications.name: Surface-specific preparation should precede competition
training_implications.recommendation: Before surface-specific events, rehearse movement, footwear, bounce timing, rally patterns, and recovery strategies on that surface when possible.
training_implications.backend_rule: If target_surface differs from recent_surface, insert surface_adaptation_block.

training_implications.name: Youth training should stay multilateral and staged
training_implications.recommendation: For juniors, develop movement literacy, coordination, strength basics, age-appropriate power, and technical variety rather than early repetitive high-intent specialization.
training_implications.backend_rule: Youth plans should cap high-intent serve spikes and include movement-quality and recovery fields.

training_implications.name: Older adult progression should prioritize preparation and recovery
training_implications.recommendation: Use longer warm-ups, balance, strength, power at appropriate dose, mobility, and conservative jumps in match or serve density.
training_implications.backend_rule: For older_adult profiles, default to lower weekly progression and longer recovery spacing after high-load days.

training_implications.name: Readiness logging should happen before and after sessions
training_implications.recommendation: Capture pain by region, fatigue, sleep, soreness, confidence, session RPE, and next-day response so load rules can adapt.
training_implications.backend_rule: Require readiness_check before high-load sessions and followup_response within 24 hours when any pain score >= 3.

training_implications.name: Return-to-tennis should progress one major variable at a time
training_implications.recommendation: Do not simultaneously increase duration, serve intent, point pressure, sprint/COD demand, and match density during return.
training_implications.backend_rule: Return-stage progression should modify only one exposure_axis per stage.

training_implications.name: Aerobic work supports tournament resilience
training_implications.recommendation: Use aerobic base and low-intensity recovery sessions to support repeat-match readiness without adding excessive impact.
training_implications.backend_rule: Add aerobic_recovery option when competition_density is high or lower-limb impact needs reduction.
